title: The Only Unsolved Hijacking in US History
description:
In 1971, a man in a suit hijacked a plane, collected $200,000 in cash, and jumped out over the Pacific Northwest. He was never seen again.

Sources: FBI's official case history on the D.B. Cooper hijacking; HistoryLink.org's account of the 1980 ransom money discovery.

#shorts #truestory #unsolvedmystery

scenes.text: On 24/11/1971, a man in a business suit boards a flight from Portland to Seattle, using the name Dan Cooper.
Mid-flight, he hands a flight attendant a note. He has a bomb, and he wants two hundred thousand dollars and four parachutes.
The airline pays. Cooper releases all thirty six passengers in Seattle, and orders the plane back into the air, heading for Mexico.
Somewhere over the dense forests of southwest Washington, he lowers the plane's rear stairs and jumps into a storm, alone, at night.
He was never found. No body, no parachute, nothing. To this day it's the only unsolved commercial hijacking in US history.
In 1980, a boy playing by the Columbia River dug up three rotting bundles of cash. Only 294 of the ten thousand bills were ever recovered.
